Compare all generated integer dots to independent int64 sums, generated/captured complete scores to canonical GPU scores plus independent CPU dots, every prepared byte, immutable input and guard. implementation: Headroom5 limits each integer operand to8160 and its16-product signed dot to1065369600. One zero-C FP16 WMMA estimates the dot and one IU8 WMMA supplies its exact low byte. Guarded nearest-class recovery, per-term discarded sums and original BF16 exception compensation use32-bit arithmetic. The complete aligned group uses unsigned modulo accumulation and the original sign disambiguation because sixteen aligned products plus carry can exceed INT32_MAX. Conditional recovery failures and unsupported rows retain original scalar replay. Every sequential normalization is preserved. Three16/32/64-column schedules share operands and both matrix outputs through LDS; the original116-byte row is unchanged.
correctness_scope: The recovery lemma still requires absolute native error below128; bounded integer arithmetic does not prove that hardware condition. Native generated integer checks observe maximum error28 with no recovery failures. All generated/captured QK score bits compare to original complete canonical GPU scores plus independent CPU dot checks. The original immutable capture provenance and comparable golden component are attached; no new GB10 model request or token-loop result is created. The q8192 component repeats1023 original rows. Counts across variants and attempts include repeated input identities and masked score slots. Every warmup and measured output, prepared input encoding, original operand, guard and unused score tail is checked. Reference outputs are comparison data only.
timing_scope: Core-only sequences compare to original four-IU8 reconstruction with one warmup and three rotated attempts, but exclude canonical carries and exceptions and time preparation separately. Full QK includes those operations, query encoding in every slab timer and one key encoding. The selected prepared control includes Q/K preparation. Full variants rotate across slabs and each receives one warmup plus three completed measurements. Allocation, reset and validation are outside component clocks; all bounded process walls and source/binary identities are attached. No probability, PV, model load, TTFT or token generation is measured.

decision.decision: Keep isolated; all original raw QK and native integer checks pass, but every candidate layout is more than twice as slow as the selected prepared QK. The32-bit specialization improves some short integer-only sequences while failing to reduce complete QK cost. Original BF16 compensation and shared data movement remain in the full measurement. No product integration or performance acceptance.
